title: Commercial Fusion Energy in 2026
subtitle: What six independent sources show about U.S. policy, ITER assembly, and the unresolved tritium and materials gaps

slides.title: Fusion in 2026: Engineering Gaps, Not Physics, Set the Pace
bullets: Deployment by mid-2030s hinges on materials and tritium breeding [S2]
ITER has placed two-thirds of its core; 28 U.S. companies tracked [S2][S4]
slides.notes: Framing: the physics case for fusion is old news — research began in the 1940s [S6] — and the 2026 story is the engineering and industrialization work. CRS R48866 (February 27, 2026) is the congressional primer on fusion technology approaches, DOE and NSF programs, ITER, and private-sector investment [S1]. Reuters (August 25, 2026) reports the U.S. government's strategy to catalyse early fusion power plants by the mid-2030s and quotes industry leaders saying success hinges on more federal funding [S2]. ITER's own release (29 July 2026) marks two-thirds of the tokamak core in place [S4]. Six active sources, six independent per the ledger; the only numeric conflict is the company count, handled on slide 7. Note the deck never quotes private-investment dollar totals: the supplied excerpts from S1 omit the private-investment figures, so those are unverified here.

slides.title: Three Numbers Define the Starting Line
bullets: No private developer has yet achieved net energy gain [S2]
slides.notes: The 28 figure is tied to a named Fusion Industry Association 2026 dataset quoted by Reuters; ANS rounds it to 'around 30' [S2][S3]. ITER's sixth-of-nine module was installed on 28 July 2026, almost six months ahead of schedule [S4]. The mid-2030s deployment aim is the U.S. government strategy described by Reuters, with the June DOE Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap as its central plank [S2]. Net energy gain status: 'Private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain' [S2]; separately, as of 2025 NIF is the only laboratory to have demonstrated a fusion energy gain factor above one [S6]. Those are different claims about different facilities and should not be conflated when speaking.

slides.title: Physics Is Proven; Materials, Tritium and Net Gain Are Not

left: No private developer has reached net energy gain [S2]
Tritium must be bred in blankets [S2][S6]

slides.notes: Left column is the current bottleneck as the sources describe it: developers must move from experimental physics to commercial net energy gain, facing neutron-resistant structural materials that survive extreme heat and breeding blankets to secure tritium supply [S2]; tritium is scarce and decays, which is why future reactors are expected to breed their own [S2][S6]. Right column is the stated target: the DOE roadmap sets concrete short, medium and long-term milestones for structural materials, plasma-facing components and fuel processing [S2]. Important nuance for the audience: ITER is primarily an exploratory science initiative and is not designed or intended to produce electricity, though it develops technology for a future demonstration plant [S1]. So ITER milestone progress is not a commercial-electricity milestone, and the deck keeps those separate.

slides.title: Four Technical Fronts Carry the Commercial Case
bullets: Inertial confinement: NIF alone above gain factor one [S6]
Breeding blankets: lithium breeds scarce tritium [S2][S6]
slides.notes: Each card is a workstream, not a vendor. Magnetic confinement (tokamak) and inertial confinement are the two approaches CRS walks through [S1]; ANS notes tokamak and laser approaches among the roughly 30 U.S. companies [S3]. Inertial confinement's data point: as of 2025 NIF is the only laboratory to demonstrate a gain factor above one, but efficiencies orders of magnitude higher are required for engineering and economic breakeven [S6]. Tritium: future reactors are expected to rely on lithium breeding blankets because tritium is scarce and decays — the ledger records this as agreed ground across sources [S2][S6]. Materials: neutron-resistant structural materials and components surviving intense neutron bombardment are a central unsolved engineering challenge, also agreed ground [S2]. AI and advanced computing appear in the DOE strategy as an acceleration lever [S2]; CRS has a section on the intersection of AI and fusion, but the supplied excerpt does not give its details, so no claim is made here.

slides.title: ITER Assembly Accelerates: Sixth Module In, Final Due 2027

stages.label: 28 July 2026
stages.detail: Sixth of nine modules placed, six months early [S4]

bullets: Three sectors on gravity supports enabled welding prep [S3]
slides.notes: Transformation per stage: from a first-of-its-kind transfer to a repeatable, faster lift sequence. ITER says teams have been installing sector modules since April 2025 and that experience from each operation increased pace, efficiency and predictability [S4]; Director-General Pietro Barabaschi called six modules in place a visible marker of the accelerated assembly approach [S4]. The sixth module was about 1,100 tonnes, weighed nearly 1,400 tonnes with its lifting rig, and the lift took 30 hours, concluding 28 July [S4]. ANS adds: vacuum vessel sector 6 was transferred in May, two more sectors followed over the summer including sector 5 in August, and with three sectors on gravity supports ITER confirmed the configuration was stable enough to begin welding preparations; sector 3 carries 120 sensors for magnetic-field measurement [S3]. The sixth module is built around vacuum vessel sector #1, the fourth and final sector made in the Republic of Korea — four of nine sectors are Korean, five European [S4]. Owner: ITER Organization.

slides.title: ITER Proves Feasibility; Private Firms Chase the Grid

left: U.S., EU, China, India, Japan, Russia, Korea collaborate [S1]
Exploratory science; not designed to produce electricity [S1]
Six of nine core modules installed [S4]
right: No net energy gain yet demonstrated [S2]
Several claim grid connection as early as the 2030s [S3]

slides.notes: The comparison is about purpose, not prestige. ITER is a multibillion-dollar collaboration among the United States, the EU as host, China, India, Japan, Russia and South Korea, intended to build a tokamak designed to prove the feasibility of fusion as a large-scale, carbon-free source [S1]; Europe contributes almost half the construction cost while the others share the rest equally [S1][S4]. ITER's key goal is operating at or near the ignition point of burning plasma; its instrumentation advances plasma science and tests materials, but it is not built to generate electricity [S1]. On the private side, there are 28 U.S. fusion companies as of 2026 [S2]; several of them claim to be on track to connect to the grid as early as the 2030s [S3], while private developers have not yet achieved net energy gain [S2]. The claim and the demonstrated status sit in the same source set and the gap is the story.

slides.title: One Real Tension: 28 Versus 'Around 30' U.S. Companies
bullets: S2: 28 U.S. companies, tied to FIA 2026 dataset [S2]
S3: 'around 30' — described as an explicit rounding [S3]
Leans to S2: same tally, slightly different moment [S2][S3]
Agreed: ITER two-thirds core; tritium breeding needed [S2][S3][S4]
slides.notes: This is the only numeric conflict in the ledger, and it is small. Reuters says 28 U.S. fusion companies as of 2026 [S2]; ANS says there are 'around 30' U.S. fusion companies, several of which claim grid connection as early as the 2030s [S3]. Weighing: the ledger leans toward S2 because its figure is specific and tied to a named Fusion Industry Association 2026 dataset, while S3's 'around 30' is an explicit rounding — the two plausibly reflect the same tally at slightly different moments rather than a real disagreement about growth. We show both positions and do not compute a single reconciled number. Stable ground, stated once: ITER had six of nine tokamak sector modules installed by late July 2026, about two-thirds of the core in place [S3][S4]; future reactors are expected to rely on lithium breeding blankets because tritium is scarce and decays [S2][S6]; neutron-resistant structural materials remain a central unsolved engineering challenge [S2]. Independence: six active, six independent sources, so the ITER agreement comes from the ITER Organization and an ANS report of ITER's own update — one underlying voice, not two independent confirmations.

slides.title: Assembly Beat Its Schedule; the Machine Is Two-Thirds Built
bullets: The 28 July lift took 30 hours; final module due 2027 [S4]
slides.notes: These are the physical proof points behind the schedule claim. ITER: the sixth of nine sector modules was lowered into the pit on 28 July 2026, almost six months ahead of schedule, in a 30-hour operation; the module was about 1,100 tonnes and the suspended load with rig nearly 1,400 tonnes; the final module is on track for 2027 [S4]. ANS corroborates the sixth-of-nine milestone and the two-thirds plasma chamber framing, and notes sectors 6, 5 and part of the summer campaign progressed on their gravity supports [S3]. Caveat to say out loud: this is assembly progress on an exploratory science machine that is not designed to produce electricity [S1], so it should not be read as evidence that commercial electricity is six months closer.

slides.title: Federal Strategy Rests on Three DOE Goals Plus ITER
bullets: Goal 1: infrastructure to close materials and technology gaps [S2]
Goal 2: AI and advanced computing access [S2]
Goal 3: partnerships for supply chain and workforce [S2]
Office of Fusion, created November 2025, coordinates delivery [S2]
slides.notes: Four cards map the federal architecture as the sources describe it. The DOE Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap released in June is the central plank of the strategy to help developers overcome materials and tritium challenges, and the Office of Fusion, created in November 2025, coordinates implementation [S2]. The strategy's three stated goals: build infrastructure to close fusion materials and technology gaps; facilitate access to AI, advanced computing and research facilities; leverage public-private partnerships to expand supply chain and workforce [S2]. It sets concrete short, medium and long-term milestones for structural materials, plasma-facing components and fuel processing [S2]. CRS supplies the congressional frame: DOE and NSF fusion R&D programs, DOE fusion energy user facilities, and ITER participation [S1]. The supplied CRS excerpt does not give FY2025 dollar figures, so this deck states no federal funding totals; industry leaders quoted by Reuters say success hinges on more federal funding [S2].

slides.title: Timeline: Roadmap 2026, Final Module 2027, Deployment Mid-2030s

Final ITER sector module — ITER Organization [S4]

stages.label: Mid-2030s
stages.detail: U.S. early plant deployment target — DOE, industry [S2]

slides.notes: Swimlane owners are named on each stage. November 2025: the Office of Fusion is created [S2]. June 2026: the DOE Fusion Science and Technology Roadmap is released, setting short, medium and long-term milestones [S2]. July–September 2026: sixth of nine ITER sector modules installed 28 July almost six months ahead of schedule, final module on track for 2027 [S4]; ANS reports sector 3 work and instrumentation with 120 sensors in September [S3]. 2027: final module positioning targeted [S4]. Mid-2030s: U.S. strategy to catalyse deployment of early-stage fusion power plants, contingent on funding per industry leaders [S2]. Two unowned uncertainties worth flagging: which private developer reaches net energy gain first is not settled by any source here, and the private-investment totals in the CRS private-investment section fall outside the supplied excerpt, so no figure is offered [S1].

slides.title: Three Numbers to Watch: 28 Firms, 9 Modules, Mid-2030s
bullets: Test for the field: first net-energy-gain device and working breeding blanket [S2]
Unsettled: which private claim reaches the grid first [S2][S3]
slides.notes: Close on the three numbers the whole deck hangs on: 28 U.S. fusion companies as of 2026, with ANS's 'around 30' rounding shown rather than smoothed away [S2][S3]; six of nine ITER sector modules now in the pit, final one targeted for 2027 [S4]; and the mid-2030s U.S. deployment aim, which industry leaders say depends on more federal funding [S2]. The field's real test is engineering: neutron-resistant structural materials, plasma-facing components and fuel processing, including tritium breeding blankets [S2]. The sources do not settle which private developer reaches net energy gain or the grid first — S3 records only that several claim grid connection as early as the 2030s — and they do not settle federal funding levels in the supplied excerpts [S1][S3]. Say that plainly rather than projecting a winner.
